findings.issue: The spent ADORE test rows are never subtracted. §2 asserts "No spent block — the ADORE t-F2F occurrence test or the prospective set — is re-scored, re-trained on or re-claimed", but the builder subtracts only (a) the six T2 classes and (b) the 11,437 prospective result_ids. Rows of the already-scored ADORE test partitions therefore sit in BOTH the new T1_test block (a second claim on spent rows) and train_pool (training on a spent test block), against sota_campaign rule 1 and RESEARCH_PLAN §15.5 items 1 and 7.
findings.evidence: Builder /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_runs/chemtox/arch_v2/build_t1t6_split.py lines 50 and 61 are the only subtractions. Spent blocks named in docs/preregistration/chemtox_test_plan.md lines 16–22 (primary t-F2F/split_occurrence; secondaries t-F2F/split_scaffold-murcko, t-C2C/split_occurrence, a-CA2F-diff/split_occurrence), all with scored registry rows (results/registry.jsonl: 90 rows for t-F2F/split_occurrence across adore_chemtox_test / adore_published_baseline / adore_trivial_baselines). Join of their test result_ids (sentinel_data/processed/adore/split_assignments.parquet) with the sealed split (chemtox_t1t6_split_v1.parquet), keys only: 11,157 spent test result_ids → 10,473 rows inside the sealed universe = 2,465 of T1_test (23.4%) and 8,008 of train_pool (13.4%), 1,477 chemicals, 1,166 clusters. For the §15.2 primary block alone (t-F2F/split_occurrence, 4,133 ids): 3,772 rows → 913 in T1_test, 2,859 in train_pool. Prospective subtraction verified exact (0 of 11,437 remain).
findings.suggested_ruling: Before any stamp the builder must also subtract, by result_id, the union of every ADORE test partition already scored (t-F2F/split_occurrence, t-F2F/split_scaffold-murcko, t-C2C/split_occurrence, a-CA2F-diff/split_occurrence, plus a-CA2F-same and t-A2A if any look exists), freeze that id list with its own sha256 in §2, and re-derive the partition, counts, §3 table and all MDEs from the reduced universe; no T1/T6 block or training pool may contain a row of a spent block.

findings.section: §3 partition table (SD(target), Replicate floor columns); §6 "From counts and metadata only"; §13
findings.issue: Label values of the sealed blocks have already been read and published. §3 prints SD(target) and the pooled within-group replicate floor for T1_test / T6a_test / T6b_test, and the pinned MDE report records sd_target for every block and stratum. LEAD_DECISIONS rule 2 allows "labels of protected rows: counts only"; §13 itself claims nothing beyond "the row counts in §3" may be read. §6's "no label of any future test row informed any number in this table" is true only of the MDE column.
findings.evidence: build_t1t6_split.py lines 147–154 (block_stats computes sd_target from log10_conc_mol_L) and lines 186–193 (per-test-block replicate_floor from the same column); compute_t1t6_mde.py line 22 loads the label-carrying partition, line 24 asserts the target column exists, line 73 writes sd_target per case (12 occurrences in t1t6_mde.json; 9 label-derived keys in t1t6_counts.json). The MDE itself is provably target-invariant (unseen_taxa.py lines 663–683: pA−y = eA, so y cancels) and the 1e-12 zeroed-target assertion at compute_t1t6_mde.py lines 64–69 is genuine, so only the SD/replicate-floor figures are affected.
findings.suggested_ruling: The stamp is withheld until §3 and §6 carry no label-derived statistic of T1_test, T6a_test or T6b_test (drop the SD(target) and per-test-block replicate-floor columns; the train_pool replicate floor may stay) and the pinned counts/MDE reports are re-emitted without sd_target and per-block replicate_floor; the breach is recorded, and no further label-derived quantity of a sealed block may be computed before its FREEZE file exists.

findings.section: §2 frozen-artefact table (rows 2–4: split file, builder, counts report)
findings.issue: The pinned builder does not produce the pinned artefacts, and an unguarded copy of the sealed blocks' labels exists on disk. The sealed split file is genuinely label-free (verified), but the builder hashed in §2 writes an 8-column partition that includes log10_conc_mol_L, under different filenames, and the pinned counts report points at that file in a world-readable temp directory. The §2 provenance chain ("deterministic; reproduces both files") is therefore false, and the trim step that produced the sealed file is unrecorded.
findings.evidence: build_t1t6_split.py lines 195–199 write chemtox_t1t6_partition.parquet with columns [result_id, test_cas, t1_cluster, duration_h, block, latin_name, reference_number, log10_conc_mol_L]; line 118 writes chemtox_t1_clusters.csv (not *_v1.csv). t1t6_counts.json records partition_file = /tmp/claude-1016/-home-bcheng-STOCKHOLM/dbc009e4-477d-4528-910a-e89e964c5c0f/scratchpad/t1t6/chemtox_t1t6_partition.parquet, sha256 9ef801b86207aac55bf872acfa5a2705e7158198d9a52c4d1c142c64e7736c31 — not the pinned 005f7957…; that file exists there, mode 0664, 85,746 rows, 8 columns (schema read only). The sealed /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_data/processed/chemtox_arch_v2/chemtox_t1t6_split_v1.parquet has exactly the 5 declared columns and matches 005f7957…; all six §2 hashes and the cluster-CSV hash a6e33634… match on disk.
findings.suggested_ruling: Before the stamp the author supplies a builder that deterministically emits the sealed label-free split and cluster file at their pinned paths and names (with the column trim inside it), re-pins the counts report so no artefact path lies in a temp directory, and deletes the 8-column label-carrying intermediate (and any copy), recording its removal; the stamp then re-verifies all hashes.

findings.issue: Auxiliary and multitask rows are filtered only by prospective result_id and T2 class — not by held-out cluster, parent structure or duration window. So censored acute rows (H2), chronic rows (H3), BCF rows (H4) and the ACR target (H5) carry the sealed blocks' chemicals, and in many cases the exact (CAS, species, duration) cell being tested, into training for ted, R2, R3, mmoe and A4/A5. This destroys T1's "a chemical nobody has tested" premise and gives T6 long-duration coverage of the pool chemicals.
findings.evidence: Counts from processed/ecotox/ecotox_aquatic.parquet keyed against the sealed split (keys only): 45,133 chronic rows on 466 held-out-cluster chemicals; 1,646 censored acute rows on held-out-cluster chemicals; auxiliary rows in the SAME (CAS, species, duration) cell as a sealed row — T1_test 4,602 chronic + 341 censored, T6a_test 11,329 + 502, T6b_test 2,119 + 72; 84,890 chronic uncensored rows above 96 h on 988 train_pool chemicals, max duration 26,298 h (identical to T6a's maximum); ACR-identifiable (chemical, species) pairs whose acute side includes a sealed row: 3,778. §9's own numbers show 588 of 672 H4 chemicals in the universe but only 456 in the pool, i.e. 132 BCF chemicals exist only in sealed blocks. Project precedent is stricter: sentinel/models/chemtox/aux.py lines 3–11 plus excluded_keys/assert_no_test_chemicals exclude by CAS and InChIKey every chemical in any test partition because "the ADORE core *is* ECOTOX, so without the exclusion this would be pure leakage". Reproduced H2 = 11,719 and H3 = 225,081 exactly, so the §10.1 target counts are the unfiltered ones.
findings.suggested_ruling: Every auxiliary, multitask, pretraining and ablation row set (H2, H3, H4, H5, R2, R3, mmoe, A4, A5) is restricted to chemicals of retained clusters, excludes every parent_key family that touches a held-out cluster, and excludes any row sharing a (CAS, species, duration) cell with a sealed row; the H5 ACR target is computed from train_pool rows only; the filtered row counts replace the §10.1 figures before the stamp, and §3/§7.1's "the pool is in-window only, selection extrapolates at most 2×" is corrected to state the duration coverage the auxiliary rows actually give.

findings.issue: There is no choke-point reader for the new blocks, and the guard §8 relies on cannot serve them. unseen_taxa_guard is hard-wired to T2 (three block names, test_blocks.parquet, the T2 plan and pins, EXPERIMENT chemtox_unseen_taxa_test); load_test_block("T1_test") raises KeyError. The guard and unseen_taxa.py are pinned by T2's live freeze, so editing them would break T2's pending look — and the amendment's own preamble promises both keep their bytes. Worse, because the sealed split is label-free, the sealed rows' labels stay in ecotox_aquatic.parquet, which many modules read directly, so no "only reader" exists for them at all.
findings.evidence: sentinel/models/chemtox/unseen_taxa_guard.py lines 34–38 (PLAN/PINS/DATA_DIR/EXPERIMENT/BLOCKS), line 103 (`if block not in BLOCKS: raise KeyError`), line 171 (reads only test_blocks.parquet), lines 91–98 (verify_freeze refuses if guard or module sha changed); docs/preregistration/chemtox_unseen_taxa_pins.json pins guard_sha256 e3721450… and module_sha256 cf1493c6…, both equal to the current files. No T1/T6 code exists (`find . -name "*chemtox*"` shows no arch-v2 module or script; sentinel_runs/chemtox/arch_v2 holds only the six reports/scripts). `grep -rln ecotox_aquatic --include=*.py` returns 7 direct readers, including sentinel/models/chemtox/aux.py and prospective.py.
findings.suggested_ruling: No fit or look on T1/T6 is cleared by this stamp until a separate guard module (new file, its own pins file, its own experiment key, the lead-written FREEZE check, BaseException abort, import-closure code hash, artefact verification and sealing) plus a protected labels file holding only the three blocks' targets exist and are reviewed; unseen_taxa_guard.py and unseen_taxa.py are not edited, and every T1/T6 training loader must read rows through the new guard's pool loader rather than ecotox_aquatic.parquet.

findings.issue: Pre-existing pretrained encoders and auxiliary caches would leak the sealed blocks. The in-tree ECOTOX encoder pretraining excludes chemicals only against an ADORE challenge's test partitions and the current validation fold, and twenty cached checkpoints predate the split. Re-using any of them to initialise ted or rx_chemprop puts T1_test/T6a/T6b rows into pretraining. (The frozen CheMeleon / MoLFormer / ChemBERTa embeddings are label-free and structure-only, so they leak no label; their structural coverage of the held-out clusters is a disclosure, not a leak.)
findings.evidence: sentinel/models/chemtox/chemprop_model.py lines 136–192 (pretrain_ecotox_encoder, cache $SENTINEL_RUNS/chemtox/pretrained/ecotox_mp_<key>.pt) and lines 325–327 ("filtered again against the current validation fold's chemicals"); sentinel/models/chemtox/aux.py lines 181–226 (ecotox_auxiliary excludes only excluded_keys(primary_challenge)). /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/sentinel_runs/chemtox/pretrained holds 20 ecotox_mp_*.pt files dated 2026-10-22, i.e. built 19 days before the T1/T6 split existed.
findings.suggested_ruling: No checkpoint, embedding cache or auxiliary row set built before the T1/T6 split may initialise or feed any T1/T6 fit: pretraining rows are re-derived from block == train_pool after the CT-L4 exclusions, the cache key records the split file's sha256, and the amendment states that the frozen pretrained embeddings saw the held-out structures (no labels) as a disclosed limitation.

findings.issue: The hold-out unit is the ECFP4 cluster of one canonical SMILES per test_cas, so salt, counter-ion and stereoisomer variants of the same parent structure can fall on both sides of the T1 split. 11.1% of T1_test rows share a parent structure with the training pool, so those rows are not novel chemistry. The project already identified and instrumented this problem for the prospective track; the amendment does not mention parent_key at all.
findings.evidence: Using the project's own helper sentinel.models.chemtox.prospective.parent_keys over chemtox_t1_clusters_v1.csv: 34 parent_keys span held-out and retained clusters, covering 130 chemicals and 92 clusters; joined to the sealed split that is 1,170 T1_test rows, 345 T6b_test rows and 1,881 T6a_test rows against 5,320 train_pool rows. Precedent: docs/preregistration/chemtox_prospective_plan.md §4.5 (49 of 301 CAS in 18 multi-CAS parent-structure groups; parent-clustered sensitivity CI pre-registered). `grep -n parent docs/preregistration/chemtox_arch_v2_amendment.md` returns nothing.
findings.suggested_ruling: Hold out whole parent_key families with their clusters and re-derive the partition; if the lead prefers to keep the current split, the amendment must pre-register, before the stamp, a parent-structure-clustered co-primary CI and a "parent-unseen" stratum (with its row counts and MDE), and every T1/T6b claim must hold in that stratum.

findings.section: §8 "One look per block, ever"; §12.1 (c) and (e); §12.2 rule 8
findings.issue: T1_test and T6b_test are built from the same 490 held-out clusters, so a look at T1 reveals the model's error on exactly T6b's chemicals. The amendment fixes no ordering of the three looks, does not require all three FREEZE files and all frozen configurations (winners, seeds, ensemble members, the 0.05 margin) to exist before the first look, and applies Holm only within a block — giving three independent chances at a §15.1 label on overlapping chemistry.
findings.evidence: §2 "490 held-out clusters"; §3 table (T1_test 468 of those clusters, T6b_test 203); sealed split confirms 727 chemicals shared between T1_test and T6b_test and 0 rows shared. §12.1(c) "Holm correction across the candidate family within that block"; §8 gives each block "its own FREEZE file and its own claim marker" with no ordering rule.
findings.suggested_ruling: All three blocks' configurations, seeds, ensemble members and comparator choices are frozen, and all three FREEZE files are issued by the lead, before the first look; no refit, re-selection or ensemble change may occur between the three looks, and Holm runs across the three blocks' primary comparisons as one family.

findings.issue: The power claim is wrong for T6b and the block's status contradicts the approved plan. §6 says "Every block is better powered than T2's best (0.011)", but T6b's primary MDE is 0.0197 — worse than T2's best (0.011) and essentially equal to T2's middle block (0.019). Plan §7.2 pre-registered that T6b, if underpowered, "is reported as a stratum of T6a, never as a separate claim"; kill rule 8 instead fixes T6b as a full block with its own look, which buys a third claim opportunity on the weakest block.
findings.evidence: §6 table rows for T6b_test: 0.0197 (ρ=0.9) primary, 0.0213 co-primary, 0.0241 / 0.0232 in the no-shared-reference stratum; verified identical in t1t6_mde.json. T2's MDEs 0.011 / 0.019 / 0.021 per docs/plans/architecture_research/M4_architecture_plan.md §7.1. Plan §7.2: "Much smaller; power must be computed before it is adopted, and if it is underpowered it is reported as a stratum of T6a, never as a separate claim."
findings.suggested_ruling: Correct the sentence to "T1 and T6a are better powered than T2's best; T6b is not", and T6b carries no §15.1 label: it is reported as a pre-declared stratum of T6a inside T6a's single look, as plan §7.2 requires, unless the lead grants it block status in writing with its own place in the Holm family.

findings.issue: The T6 blocks contain physically impossible and sub-hour durations, and the long tail that carries the headline "274×" is very thin. Nothing in the file pre-registers a minimum admissible duration or per-band row counts, so dropping the degenerate rows, or choosing which band the claim rests on, remains available after the look.
findings.evidence: Sealed split, keys only: duration_h == 0 in 2 T6a_test rows and 1 T6b_test row; 0 < duration_h < 1 h in 337 T6a_test and 84 T6b_test rows; pre-registered band occupancy — T6a lt24 4,522 / 96_168 3,893 / 168_720 4,252 / 720_2160 343 / gt2160 49, T6b 964 / 608 / 769 / 50 / 19. §3 reports only "5,486 below 24 h, 9,983 above 96 h" and "maximum 26,298 h"; the MDE bands (compute_t1t6_mde.py line 28, edge −0.001) absorb the zero-duration rows silently.
findings.suggested_ruling: Before the stamp the amendment must state the minimum admissible duration (drop duration_h ≤ 0 and declare the treatment of < 1 h), publish the per-band row counts for T6a and T6b, and pre-declare the short tail (< 24 h) and long tail (> 96 h) as separately reported strata, with no claim resting on a band whose row count is below a number fixed now.

findings.issue: R5 cannot satisfy claim condition (a) and its pre-look read touches the sealed chemistry. TRIDENT's released file gives per-SMILES errors from TRIDENT's own 10×10 CV on TRIDENT's rows, so there are no per-row predictions on our block and no paired block-bootstrap against it is computable; TRIDENT's training data overlaps our rows (the file says so) and its CV is random rather than cluster-held-out, so it is not a parity comparison; and reading its per-SMILES errors "over the intersecting SMILES" before the look exposes a difficulty ranking of the sealed chemicals. §4.3 also requires the strongest published method to be "decided by validation on the pool", which a no-fit file read cannot enter.
findings.evidence: §4.2 R5 ("via its released per-SMILES 10×10-CV errors, never by re-running TRIDENT"; "TRIDENT's training data overlaps our rows"); §5.2 "r5_trident_released_errors 1 (no fit — a read of the released file over the intersecting SMILES)"; §12.1(a) requires a "paired CI (cluster bootstrap … unit = the block's resampling unit) excluding 0 against the strongest published method on that block". Licence verified in docs/licenses.md (TRIDENT Zenodo 10260621, CC BY 4.0, cleared 2026-11-10), so admissibility is not the issue.
findings.suggested_ruling: Condition (a) is read against a published comparator re-run on our rows at input parity (mmoe or gpboost_published); the TRIDENT comparison is reported as a descriptive, non-paired, non-parity cross-reference with its split mismatch and training overlap stated, and the released per-SMILES errors are restricted to pool chemicals until the FREEZE file exists, the sealed-block intersection being read only inside the single scored pass.

findings.issue: 74.4% of T1_test rows share a publication with the training pool, so publication-level information crosses the primary split, yet condition (h) only requires the reference-clustered co-primary CI to exclude 0 and the no-shared-reference stratum to be "reported". A T1 label could therefore rest almost entirely on rows whose study is already in training.
findings.evidence: §3: shared-reference row share 74.4% (T1_test), 53.8% (T6a), 30.9% (T6b) — reproduced from t1t6_counts.json (0.7443 / 0.5382 / 0.3087); no-shared-reference rows 2,697 / 6,031 / 1,666 with stratum MDEs 0.0167 / 0.0134 / 0.0241 (§6). T2's comparable share was 16–29%. There is no temporal or publication-date rule anywhere in the file.
findings.suggested_ruling: A §15.1 label on T1 (and on T6a/T6b) additionally requires the no-shared-reference stratum's point difference to have the same sign as the primary and to exceed that stratum's ρ=0.9 MDE; otherwise the result is reported as "competitive" and any label is explicitly scoped as including shared-publication rows.

findings.issue: The three new blocks are reserved only inside this amendment. The lead's pattern for every other round-v2 reservation (M2 Test-S, M5-F, M1-SP, M7 P2) is an entry in sota_campaign.md's "Reserved unseen blocks" list so other workstreams exclude the rows.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/sota_campaign.md sections "Reserved unseen blocks (lead, 2026-11-09)" and "Reserved unseen blocks added 2026-11-10" list M2/M5/M1/M7 blocks; grep of that file finds no chemtox T1/T6 entry. Amendment §8 reserves them only by reference to chemtox_t1t6_split_v1.parquet.
findings.suggested_ruling: At the stamp the lead adds T1_test, T6a_test and T6b_test to sota_campaign.md's reserved-blocks list, naming the split file and its sha256 005f7957…, with the standing instruction that no workstream trains or tunes on those result_ids.

findings.issue: What checked out, recorded so the lead need not re-verify: the parts of the design that are sound are sound.
findings.evidence: File sha256 b9326d49… matches the author's. All eight §2 hashes match on disk (cluster CSV a6e33634…, split 005f7957…, builder, counts, MDE, MDE script, H4 report, H4 script) and the sealed split carries exactly the five declared columns, 85,746 rows. Every count in §2/§3 reproduces (122,946 / 4,592 / 2,550; −24,219 → 98,727; −11,437 → 87,290; 18 unparseable rows, 2 chemicals; 85,746 / 3,895 / 1,572 / 6,656; 2,603 clusters, 2,067 singletons, largest 4,577 = 5.34%; 490 held-out clusters; blocks 59,729 / 10,548 / 13,059 / 2,410; T1_test = 15.01% of in-window rows; out-of-window 18.04%; fold rows 14,334+15,945+14,325+15,125 = 59,729 and clusters 439+432+566+542 = 1,979). The T2 class exclusion is a true superset of T2's blocks and no frozen artefact is opened (builder lines 28–30, 50 vs unseen_taxa.py lines 51–58). Prospective subtraction exact. Partition is row-disjoint and no (CAS, species, duration, endpoint) group spans two blocks (0 of 43,020); held-out and pool chemicals disjoint on both CAS forms. Every §6 MDE matches t1t6_mde.json and the statistic is provably target-invariant. H2 = 11,719, H3 = 225,081 and the §9 H4 figures (17,418 / 672 / 479; 588 / 456) reproduce. Licences match docs/licenses.md. Registry: no chemtox row for T1/T6/arch_v2, and chemtox_unseen_taxa_test has 0 rows, so T2's blocks are unspent. Caps arithmetic 384 + 11 + 128 + 9 + 12 = 544 across 38 entries is internally consistent and within the lead's caps, with comparators given the same per-entry budget as candidates.
findings.suggested_ruling: No action; the lead can rely on these checks and need only re-verify the items changed by CT-L1 to CT-L4 (which force a rebuild of the partition, the counts and all MDEs).

points.point: The disclosed T6 extrapolation decision: pool in-window only, so selection extrapolates at most 2× while the test blocks reach 274×; the alternative (long tail in the pool) was rejected.
points.recommendation: Accept the design (keeping the long tail out of the pool is the stricter choice), but rule that the disclosure as written is false and must be corrected before the stamp: the auxiliary chronic rows the same amendment admits give the training set duration coverage to 26,298 h on 988 pool chemicals, so the pool is not in-window once H3 enters. Require the amendment to state the duration coverage of every row set (primary, auxiliary, pretraining) separately, to apply CT-L4's exclusions, and to pre-register the short (<24 h) and long (>96 h) tails plus per-band counts as fixed strata so no band can be chosen after the look.
points.reason: The only reason the 2×-versus-274× disclosure protects anything is that the training set is supposed to carry no long-duration information. Measured: 84,890 chronic rows above 96 h on pool chemicals, 11,329 of them in the same (CAS, species, duration) cell as a T6a_test row. The claim would otherwise rest on a shape the model had in fact seen, and the long tail that justifies "274×" is only 49 rows in T6a and 19 in T6b.

points.point: The 544-configuration total (384 + 11 + 128 + 9 + 12 across 38 entries) against the §8.2 caps.
points.recommendation: Approve the count as declared: 512 searched is exactly the lead's 384 (T1) + 128 (T6), the 32 remaining are fixed baselines and the 12 pre-declared ablations, and no entry exceeds its track's per-entry cap. Add one binding sentence that the 12 ablation fits count inside the fixed allowance and may not grow if the pre-declared fallback cuts ted to 8 configurations, and that the realised count, including failures and discarded configurations, is reconciled against these five figures in the write-up and on every registry row.
points.reason: The arithmetic and the entry lists check out (12×32 = 384, 11 fixed across 10 entries, 8×16 = 128, 9 fixed across 8 entries, 6 ablations per track; 22 + 16 = 38 entries), and comparators receive the same per-entry budget as candidates, which is what rule 3 parity needs. The only soft edge is that ablations are fits of ted not named in the lead's cap sentence, which one sentence closes.

points.point: T5 (cross-source transfer) blocked on the EnviroTox licence; TRIDENT Zenodo 10260621 cleared so R5 is admissible.
points.recommendation: Uphold both: record T5 as blocked, not skipped, and forbid any EnviroTox retrieval or overlap audit until written HESI permission is in docs/licenses.md. Admit R5 as a licensed data read only, and couple it to the CT-L11 ruling: R5 cannot carry claim condition (a), and its per-SMILES errors must not be read over the sealed blocks' chemicals before the FREEZE file exists.
points.reason: The licence findings match docs/licenses.md exactly (TRIDENT CC BY 4.0, open, 35.7 MB of 10 GB; EnviroTox has no terms page and an all-rights-reserved notice). Blocking T5 removes a leakage surface rather than creating one. The residual risk is on the R5 side: the admissible file is a label-derived per-chemical error table from a model whose training data overlaps our sealed rows, so its admissibility as data is not admissibility as the paired comparator.

summary: Hash matches (b9326d49…). Counts, hashes, MDEs and the T2-class exclusion all reproduce, and the four-way partition is row-disjoint. But five blocking leakage defects remain: 2,465 T1_test and 8,008 train_pool rows belong to already-scored ADORE test blocks; test-block label statistics (SD, replicate floor) were already computed and published; the pinned builder emits an undocumented label-carrying partition that still sits in a temp directory; auxiliary chronic/censored/BCF/ACR rows carry sealed chemicals and cells into training; and no guard can serve the new blocks, since unseen_taxa_guard is pinned to T2. Seven should_fix items cover parent-structure leakage, pretrained-encoder reuse, look ordering, T6b power, degenerate durations, R5 and shared references. Do not stamp as written.
